page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-8GB is a virtual server belonging to the Starter family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 40 GB of local SSD storage. It also comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier. However, multi-core and multi-threaded performance is more limited, as evidenced by an average multi-core stress-ng score and a weak rating for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Passmark CPU and memory scores are also positioned in the lower tier, reflecting the shared CPU allocation. Memory bandwidth remains average across both small and large block read and write tests.

The primary tradeoff of this server is its shared CPU allocation, which limits sustained multi-threaded performance despite the high-performing AMD EPYC architecture. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for entry-level workloads that benefit from strong single-core bursts but do not require dedicated, continuous multi-core compute. Suitable workloads include static web serving, lightweight Redis caching, and basic application hosting, whereas resource-intensive database operations or medium-to-large language model inference are not recommended due to weak benchmark results in those areas.
